arrival_context: A Google search for 'marriage licence' while comparing destination planners

first_impression.reaction: Good. It answers the question in the first sentence, puts a date on it, links the Attorney-General's Department and says it isn't legal advice. Nobody's selling me anything yet. I jumped to the FAQ first, as I always do, and every answer there has a source. I'll keep going.

journey.quote: If you are searching for a marriage licence in Australia, there is none to apply for.
journey.reaction: A straight answer in the first sentence and no waffle. That's how I like it.

journey.quote: This is general information as at November 2026, not legal advice.
journey.reaction: It's honest about its limits and it's dated. I can check it against the government site, and I will.

journey.quote: The practical lesson: lodge the notice once your date and celebrant are settled, rather than in the final month.
journey.reaction: Useful and specific. It's the kind of thing I'd put in the spreadsheet.

journey.quote: and your celebrant can do this on your behalf, generally at a cost.
journey.reaction: I like that it admits there's a cost and doesn't pretend it's free. That's the tone I want from a planner too.

journey.section: Is a marriage licence from New Zealand or Hawaii recognised in Australia?
journey.quote: What is recognised is the marriage, not the licence.
journey.reaction: Clear distinction, backed by Smartraveller. The FAQ holds up.
It names a real trade-off of marrying overseas and doesn't gloss over it. Points for honesty.

journey.section: Marry at home and celebrate abroad
journey.quote: The paperwork stays with you, your celebrant and the registry, while a Wedded Advisor plans the venue, travel, vendors and payments anywhere in the world, as your single point of contact from start to finish.
journey.reaction: This is where the tone changes. 'Anywhere in the world' has nothing behind it, unlike the rest of the article. And 'payments' makes me ask straight away: whose account does my money go through, and do you take a cut from the venue?

journey.section: Plan your wedding abroad with Wedded Concierge
journey.quote: Plan your wedding abroad with Wedded Concierge
journey.reaction: Is Wedded Concierge a service, a person or a page? Earlier it was a Wedded Advisor. I'm not sure whether these are the same thing or two separate things I'd pay for.

journey.section: Plan your wedding abroad with Wedded Concierge
journey.quote: Whichever country makes it legal, one Wedded Advisor works in your time zone and quotes in AUD, and the fee is agreed in writing before any work begins.
journey.reaction: A written fee before any work starts is the best line in the sales part. But it's buried at the end of the sentence, and it still doesn't tell me how the fee works or whether supplier prices carry a mark-up.

journey.section: Plan your wedding abroad with Wedded Concierge
journey.quote: Tell us your date, your guest list and where you would like to marry
journey.reaction: You want my details before you've told me the fee model. Fair enough for a blog post, but I won't fill it in until I've seen the pricing page.

unanswered_questions: How is the Wedded Advisor's fee worked out: flat, percentage or something else?
Does Wedded Wonderland take commissions or mark-ups from venues and suppliers?
When it says the Advisor plans 'payments', does my money pass through Wedded Wonderland's accounts or go straight to the suppliers?
What exactly does the fee cover, and what costs extra?
Is there a real wedding I can look at with the actual budget?
Are Wedded Concierge and the Wedded Advisor the same service?

turn_offs_found.quote: while a Wedded Advisor plans the venue, travel, vendors and payments anywhere in the world, as your single point of contact from start to finish.
turn_offs_found.why: It's an unsupported sweeping claim in an article where everything else is sourced. 'Anywhere in the world' reads like marketing.

would_share_with: My fiancee, as the plain answer on the notice and the certificate
A mate weighing up New Zealand versus marrying at home first

cta_reaction.quote: Whichever country makes it legal, one Wedded Advisor works in your time zone and quotes in AUD, and the fee is agreed in writing before any work begins.
cta_reaction.why: The article earned enough trust for me to click through and look for the fee model. I wouldn't send my details from this page, because my main questions (fee structure and supplier commissions) aren't answered here. At least the CTAs come after the evidence and not before it.

top_3_changes: Drop 'anywhere in the world' from the Advisor sentence. It's the one unsupported claim in an otherwise sourced article.
Lead the closing sentence with the written fee agreement. It's the strongest trust signal for a sceptical reader and is currently buried at the end.

Make it clear how Wedded Concierge and the Wedded Advisor relate, so a reader isn't left wondering whether they're two separate paid services (wording for the business to supply, as the draft doesn't say).

suggested_edits.old: while a Wedded Advisor plans the venue, travel, vendors and payments anywhere in the world, as your single point of contact from start to finish.
suggested_edits.new: while a Wedded Advisor plans the venue, travel, vendors and payments, as your single point of contact from start to finish.
suggested_edits.why: Removes an unsupported sweeping claim and adds nothing new.

suggested_edits.old: Whichever country makes it legal, one Wedded Advisor works in your time zone and quotes in AUD, and the fee is agreed in writing before any work begins.
suggested_edits.new: Whichever country makes it legal, the fee is agreed in writing before any work begins, and one Wedded Advisor works in your time zone and quotes in AUD.
suggested_edits.why: Reorders existing facts so the written fee agreement comes first. No new claims.
